title: CTS Church Growth — Unit 9: Digital and Online Ministry

blocks.en: 📈 Church Growth — Unit 9: Digital and Online Ministry
blocks.es_reference: 📈 Crecimiento de la Iglesia — Unidad 9: Ministerio Digital y en Línea

blocks.en: Professor: Dr. Wayne Cook | Director: Dr. Ted Rogers
blocks.es_reference: Profesor: Dr. Wayne Cook | Director: Dr. Ted Rogers

blocks.en: "Go out into the highways and hedges, and compel them to come in, that my house may be filled." — Luke 14:23 (NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: "Ve por los caminos y por los vallados, y fuérzalos a entrar, para que se llene mi casa." — Lucas 14:23 (RVG)
Originalmente: El Crecimiento de la Iglesia por Medio del Telemercadeo.

blocks.en:
There was a season when the cutting edge of outreach was the
telephone. Churches ran marketing campaigns to plant and grow
congregations on a simple arithmetic of the funnel: call twenty thousand
homes, find two thousand unchurched people willing to talk, and perhaps
two hundred would show up on a given Sunday. One widely used phone
program helped start thousands of churches in just a few years. The
method was concrete: gather volunteers, work through long calling lists,
and follow up the interested with a mailing and an invitation.
blocks.es_reference: Hubo una temporada en que la vanguardia del alcance era el teléfono. Las iglesias corrían campañas de mercadeo para plantar y hacer crecer congregaciones sobre una aritmética simple del embudo: llamar a veinte mil hogares, hallar a dos mil no eclesiásticos dispuestos a hablar, y quizá doscientos se presentarían un domingo dado. Un programa telefónico muy usado ayudó a iniciar miles de iglesias en pocos años. El método era concreto: reunir voluntarios, trabajar largas listas de llamadas, y dar seguimiento a los interesados con un envío y una invitación.

blocks.en:
The numbers told the story of the funnel — and the story of
attrition. A church planter might make thirteen thousand calls to gather
perhaps thirteen hundred prospects; of those, around a hundred and
thirty would come to a first service; and then the siftings began.
Roughly a quarter fell away after the first Sunday, and a quarter of the
remainder the Sunday after that — until what was left, a faithful
seventy or so, became the core group around which a real church could be
built. Mass mailings worked the same arithmetic: a planter might gather
a small Bible study, then blanket the area with mail and see a hundred
and sixty at the first service, settling after the siftings into a
steady core, then mail again and climb higher.
blocks.es_reference: Los números contaban la historia del embudo — y la historia de la merma. Un plantador de iglesias podía hacer trece mil llamadas para reunir quizá mil trescientos prospectos; de esos, alrededor de ciento treinta vendrían a un primer servicio; y luego comenzaban los tamizados. Cerca de una cuarta parte caía después del primer domingo, y una cuarta parte del resto el domingo siguiente — hasta que lo que quedaba, unos setenta fieles, se volvía el núcleo en torno al cual una iglesia real podía edificarse. Los envíos masivos trabajaban la misma aritmética: un plantador podía reunir un pequeño estudio bíblico, luego cubrir el área con correo y ver ciento sesenta en el primer servicio, asentándose tras los tamizados en un núcleo estable, y luego enviar de nuevo y subir más alto.

blocks.en: Notice what endures in all of this, for it outlives the telephone. First, outreach at scale is a funnel: you cast widely because most will not respond, and you build on the faithful few who do. Second, the goal of the wide cast was never the crowd at the first service; it was the core group left after the siftings — the committed people on whom a church is actually built. Third, the response rates were always small, and that was not failure but the normal shape of sowing broadly to reap narrowly. The channel in this chapter — the telephone — has all but vanished. The logic of the funnel has not.
blocks.es_reference: Note lo que perdura en todo esto, pues sobrevive al teléfono. Primero, el alcance a escala es un embudo: se lanza ampliamente porque la mayoría no responderá, y se edifica sobre los pocos fieles que sí. Segundo, la meta del lanzamiento amplio nunca fue la multitud del primer servicio; era el núcleo que quedaba tras los tamizados — la gente comprometida sobre la cual una iglesia de veras se edifica. Tercero, las tasas de respuesta siempre fueron pequeñas, y eso no era fracaso sino la forma normal de sembrar ampliamente para cosechar estrechamente. El canal de este capítulo — el teléfono — casi ha desaparecido. La lógica del embudo, no.

blocks.en:
Let it be said plainly: telemarketing is dead, and so very nearly is
the mass mailing. The cold call now meets a cell phone, a do-not-call
list, and a deep weariness with strangers selling things; the mass
mailing meets a recycling bin. A church that built its outreach on phone
banks today would be pouring water into sand. But the funnel did not die
with the telephone — it simply moved, wholesale, onto the screen, and
the church that grasps this has lost a tool and gained a continent.
blocks.es_reference: Dígase llanamente: el telemercadeo está muerto, y muy casi también el envío masivo. La llamada fría ahora se topa con un celular, una lista de no-llamar, y un cansancio profundo de extraños que venden cosas; el envío masivo se topa con un cesto de reciclaje. Una iglesia que hoy edificara su alcance sobre bancos telefónicos estaría vertiendo agua en la arena. Pero el embudo no murió con el teléfono — sencillamente se mudó, por completo, a la pantalla, y la iglesia que entiende esto ha perdido una herramienta y ganado un continente.

blocks.en: The front door of the church is now digital. Long before a stranger ever parks a car, he visits — by way of the website, the livestream, the social feed, the search result, the recommended video, the podcast, the online sermon. He attends for weeks in the anonymity he craves before he is ever seen, exactly the relief from pressure the seeker movement labored to give him, now granted by a screen. So the first impression is no longer made in the parking lot; it is made online, and a church with no findable, welcoming digital presence is, to a rising generation, a church that does not exist. The new funnel runs through the feed: the wide cast is the post seen by thousands, the prospect is the one who watches to the end or clicks through, the core is the handful who finally walk in the door — the very same arithmetic the phone campaigns ran, on a scale they could never have dreamed.
blocks.es_reference: La puerta de entrada de la iglesia es ahora digital. Mucho antes de que un extraño estacione un auto, visita — por medio del sitio web, la transmisión en vivo, el muro social, el resultado de búsqueda, el video recomendado, el podcast, el sermón en línea. Asiste por semanas en el anonimato que anhela antes de ser visto, exactamente el alivio de la presión que el movimiento del buscador se esforzó por darle, ahora concedido por una pantalla. Así que la primera impresión ya no se hace en el estacionamiento; se hace en línea, y una iglesia sin una presencia digital localizable y acogedora es, para una generación en ascenso, una iglesia que no existe. El nuevo embudo corre por el muro: el lanzamiento amplio es la publicación vista por miles, el prospecto es el que la mira hasta el final o hace clic, el núcleo es el puñado que finalmente cruza la puerta — la misma aritmética que corrían las campañas telefónicas, a una escala que jamás pudieron soñar.

blocks.en: The hard turn came all at once. When the doors of the churches were shut, every congregation in the land became, overnight, a broadcast — and what began as emergency became permanent. We learned to gather partly through a screen, and many never fully came back to the pew. That has given us a genuine new field: the church’s reach, its orbit, is now far larger than the room, and a congregation can truly minister to the homebound, the distant, the curious, and the wary in ways the first edition could not have imagined.
blocks.es_reference: El giro duro vino de golpe. Cuando las puertas de las iglesias fueron cerradas, cada congregación del país se volvió, de la noche a la mañana, una transmisión — y lo que comenzó como emergencia se volvió permanente. Aprendimos a reunirnos en parte por una pantalla, y muchos nunca volvieron del todo a la banca. Eso nos ha dado un campo nuevo y genuino: el alcance de la iglesia, su órbita, es ahora mucho más grande que el salón, y una congregación puede de veras ministrar al recluido en casa, al lejano, al curioso y al receloso de maneras que la primera edición no pudo imaginar.

blocks.en: But here a warning must be sounded, and it is the deepest thing this unit has to say. The very internet that is our greatest tool of outreach is, at the same time, one of the great engines of the dechurching. The screen that lets a seeker explore the faith unseen also lets a believer drift away unseen, quietly trading the gathered body for a glowing rectangle, until faith becomes a thing watched rather than lived. The tool that gathers also scatters. So we must hold a clear conviction: the screen is a fine front porch and a poor living room. It is superb for first contact, for casting the net wide, for reaching the one who would never yet walk in — and it is no substitute at all for the embodied life of the body, the bread broken in one another’s presence, the friend who knows your name. Use the digital door to bring people in; never let it become the place they stay. An online crowd of spectators is not a church, however large the number on the screen.
blocks.es_reference: Pero aquí debe sonarse una advertencia, y es lo más profundo que esta unidad tiene que decir. El mismo internet que es nuestra mayor herramienta de alcance es, al mismo tiempo, uno de los grandes motores del abandono de la iglesia. La pantalla que deja a un buscador explorar la fe sin ser visto también deja a un creyente alejarse sin ser visto, cambiando calladamente el cuerpo reunido por un rectángulo brillante, hasta que la fe se vuelve algo observado en vez de vivido. La herramienta que reúne también dispersa. Así que debemos sostener una convicción clara: la pantalla es un buen porche de entrada y una pobre sala. Es magnífica para el primer contacto, para lanzar la red ampliamente, para alcanzar al que aun nunca entraría — y no es sustituto alguno de la vida encarnada del cuerpo, el pan partido en la presencia unos de otros, el amigo que sabe tu nombre. Use la puerta digital para traer a la gente adentro; nunca deje que se vuelva el lugar donde se queda. Una multitud en línea de espectadores no es una iglesia, por grande que sea el número en la pantalla.

blocks.en: So the funnel still runs, and the channel has simply changed. Cast wide on the screen, as our forebears cast wide on the telephone — but cast in order to gather, and gather in order to form, until the one who first found you online is finally seated at the table, known and knowing, a disciple and not a spectator. That is the next thing this course must take up.
blocks.es_reference: Así que el embudo aún corre, y el canal sencillamente ha cambiado. Lance ampliamente en la pantalla, como nuestros antecesores lanzaron ampliamente en el teléfono — pero lance para reunir, y reúna para formar, hasta que el que primero lo encontró en línea esté finalmente sentado a la mesa, conocido y conociendo, un discípulo y no un espectador. Eso es lo siguiente que este curso debe tratar.

sa.prompt: Describe the old telemarketing 'funnel' and its arithmetic. How did the campaign actually work?
sa.model: The old method was a telemarketing funnel: a church would place thousands of phone calls, sift out the few hundred who were interested, invite them, and after several siftings gather a much smaller core group that became the launch of a congregation. The arithmetic was brutal; many thousands of contacts yielded a modest core, but it worked because evangelism is a sifting of the many to find the few.

sa.prompt: Explain the principle that 'the channel died but the logic endures.' What carries over from telemarketing to today?
sa.model: The telephone channel is dead, mass cold-calling no longer works, but the funnel logic endures: reaching people still means casting wide, then patiently sifting many contacts down toward the few who become disciples. The lesson carries straight into digital ministry; only the channel changed from the phone to the screen, while the patient, narrowing work of evangelism stayed the same.

sa.prompt: Describe the church's new digital front door. What channels now serve as the first point of contact?
sa.model: The front door is now digital: the website, the livestream, social media, search results, and the podcast are where most outsiders first meet a church. People form their first impression on a screen long before they ever stand in a foyer, so the digital presence is no longer optional decoration but the actual entrance through which a watching world arrives.

sa.prompt: Why do people now 'attend anonymously' before they ever walk in, and how should a church treat such a watcher?
sa.model: Many people now watch a church online anonymously for weeks or months, testing it from a safe distance before risking a visit. Such a watcher is a guest standing on the front porch; the church should treat the online service as a real welcome, warm and clear, and give gentle on-ramps that invite the watcher to step from the screen into the gathered body.

sa.prompt: Explain the 'orbit' and why the events of 2020 forced every church to learn to count it.
sa.model: In 2020 the doors shut and nearly every church became a broadcaster overnight, discovering that its true reach was an orbit far larger than the room: people who watched, served, and belonged through a screen. The lesson stayed after the doors reopened; a church must now count the orbit as well as the pews, for many who belong never sit in the building.

sa.prompt: State the sober warning that the internet 'both gathers and scatters.' How is it an engine of dechurching?
sa.model: The same internet that can gather a watching world can also scatter it, and it has been an engine of much dechurching. It lets people replace the gathered body with a screen, drift from any congregation while feeling religiously fed, and isolate into a private, consuming faith. The tool both gathers and scatters; used carelessly it disperses the very flock it could have drawn in.

sa.prompt: Explain the image of the screen as 'front porch, not living room.' How should digital ministry be used?
sa.model: The screen is meant to be a front porch, a welcoming threshold, not the living room where a person settles in to stay. Digital ministry should be used to bring people in toward the gathered body, never to be the place they live out their whole faith. A church that lets the orbit stay forever on the porch has made spectators, not disciples.

sa.prompt: Why are online spectators 'not the church,' and what does this mean for measuring digital success?
sa.model: A crowd that only watches is an audience, not the church; the church is a gathered body of disciples who belong, serve, and share life. So digital success is not measured by view counts but by how many watchers are moved from consuming a screen into belonging to the body. A million views that make no disciples is a number, not a church.

sa.prompt: Defend the claim that the old funnel and the new screen obey the same evangelistic logic.
sa.model: Both the telemarketing funnel and the digital screen cast a wide net and then narrow it: many are reached, fewer respond, fewer still are gathered and discipled. The screen reaches more people than the phone ever could, but the logic is identical, sift the many to find and form the few. Evangelism in any age is wide contact narrowing toward committed disciples.

sa.prompt: Synthesis: How should a church use its digital front door faithfully, holding together its reach and its dangers?
sa.model: A church should use the digital front door to reach its wide orbit and welcome watchers warmly, while always building on-ramps that bring them off the screen and into the gathered body. It must resist letting the porch become the home, remembering that the internet both gathers and scatters. Used as an entrance and not a destination, the screen serves the one aim: making and gathering disciples.
